verses.zh: 以色列王以拉的儿子何细亚第三年，犹大王亚哈斯的儿子希西家登基。
verses.en: In the third year of the reign of Israel’s King Hoshea son of Elah, Ahaz’s son Hezekiah became king over Judah.

verses.zh: 他登基的时候年二十五岁，在耶路撒冷作王二十九年。他母亲名叫亚比，是撒迦利雅的女儿。
verses.en: He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] His mother[NOTE:2] was Abi,[NOTE:3] the daughter of Zechariah.
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “the name of his mother.”
The parallel passage in 2 Chr 29:1 has “Abijah.”

verses.zh: 希西家行耶和华眼中看为正的事，效法他祖大卫一切所行的。
verses.en: He did what the Lord approved, just as his ancestor David had done.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he did what was proper in the eyes of the Lord, according to all which David his father had done.”

verses.zh: 他废去邱坛，毁坏柱像，砍下木偶，打碎摩西所造的铜蛇，因为到那时以色列人仍向铜蛇烧香。希西家叫铜蛇为铜块（或译：人称铜蛇为铜像）。
verses.en: He eliminated the high places, smashed the sacred pillars to bits, and cut down the Asherah pole.[NOTE:1] He also demolished the bronze serpent that Moses had made, for up to that time[NOTE:2] the Israelites had been offering incense to it; it was called Nehushtan.[NOTE:3]
notes: Asherah was a leading deity of the Canaanite pantheon, wife/sister of El and goddess of fertility. She was commonly worshiped at shrines in or near groves of evergreen trees, or, failing that, at places marked by wooden poles. These were to be burned or cut down (Deut 12:3; 16:21; Judg 6:25, 28, 30; 2 Kgs 18:4).tn The term is singular in the MT but plural in the LXX and other ancient versions. It is also possible to regard the singular as a collective singular, especially in the context of other plural items.
Heb “until those days.”
In Hebrew the name sounds like the phrase נְחַשׁ הַנְּחֹשֶׁת (nekhash hannekhoshet), “bronze serpent.”

verses.zh: 希西家倚靠耶和华―以色列的　神，在他前后的犹大列王中没有一个及他的。
verses.en: He trusted in the Lord God of Israel; in this regard there was none like him among the kings of Judah either before or after.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and after him there was none like him among all the kings of Judah, and those who were before him.”

verses.zh: 因为他专靠耶和华，总不离开，谨守耶和华所吩咐摩西的诫命。
verses.en: He was loyal to[NOTE:1] the Lord and did not abandon him.[NOTE:2] He obeyed the commandments that the Lord had given to[NOTE:3] Moses.
notes: Heb “he hugged.”
Heb “and did not turn aside from after him.”
Heb “had commanded.”

verses.zh: 耶和华与他同在，他无论往何处去尽都亨通。他背叛、不肯事奉亚述王。
verses.en: The Lord was with him; he succeeded in all his endeavors.[NOTE:1] He rebelled against the king of Assyria and refused to submit to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in all which he went out [to do], he was successful.”
Heb “and did not serve him.”

verses.zh: 希西家攻击非利士人，直到迦萨，并迦萨的四境，从了望楼到坚固城。
verses.en: He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from watchtower to fortified city.

verses.zh: 希西家王第四年，就是以色列王以拉的儿子何细亚第七年，亚述王撒缦以色上来围困撒马利亚；
verses.en: In the fourth year of King Hezekiah’s reign (it was the seventh year of the reign of Israel’s King Hoshea, son of Elah), King Shalmaneser of Assyria marched up[NOTE:1] against Samaria[NOTE:2] and besieged it.
notes: Heb “went up” (also in v. 13).
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 过了三年就攻取了城。希西家第六年，以色列王何细亚第九年，撒马利亚被攻取了。
verses.en: After three years he captured it (in the sixth year of Hezekiah’s reign); in the ninth year of King Hoshea’s reign over Israel, Samaria was captured.

verses.zh: 亚述王将以色列人掳到亚述，把他们安置在哈腊与歌散的哈博河边，并米底亚人的城邑；
verses.en: The king of Assyria deported the people of Israel[NOTE:1] to Assyria. He settled them in Halah, along the Habor (the river of Gozan), and in the cities of the Medes.
notes: The Hebrew text has simply “Israel” as the object of the verb.

verses.zh: 都因他们不听从耶和华―他们　神的话，违背他的约，就是耶和华仆人摩西吩咐他们所当守的。
verses.en: This happened because they did not obey[NOTE:1] the Lord their God and broke his covenant with them. They did not pay attention to and obey all that Moses, the Lord’s servant, had commanded.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “listen to the voice of.”
Heb “all that Moses, the Lord’s servant, had commanded, and they did not listen and they did not act.”

verses.zh: 希西家王十四年，亚述王西拿基立上来攻击犹大的一切坚固城，将城攻取。
verses.en: In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah’s reign, King Sennacherib of Assyria marched up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

verses.zh: 犹大王希西家差人往拉吉去见亚述王，说：「我有罪了，求你离开我；凡你罚我的，我必承当。」于是亚述王罚犹大王希西家银子三百他连得，金子三十他连得。
verses.en: King Hezekiah of Judah sent this message to the king of Assyria, who was at Lachish, “I have violated our treaty.[NOTE:1] If you leave, I will do whatever you demand.”[NOTE:2] So the king of Assyria demanded that King Hezekiah of Judah pay 300 talents[NOTE:3] of silver and 30 talents of gold.
notes: Or “I have done wrong.”
Heb “Return from upon me; what you place upon me, I will carry.”

The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 22,500 pounds of silver and 2,250 pounds of gold.

verses.zh: 希西家就把耶和华殿里和王宫府库里所有的银子都给了他。
verses.en: Hezekiah gave him all the silver in[NOTE:1] the Lord’s temple and in the treasuries of the royal palace.
notes: Heb “that was found.”

verses.zh: 那时，犹大王希西家将耶和华殿门上的金子和他自己包在柱上的金子都刮下来，给了亚述王。
verses.en: At that time King Hezekiah of Judah stripped the metal overlays from the doors of the Lord’s temple and from the posts that he had plated[NOTE:1] and gave them to the king of Assyria.
notes: Heb “At that time Hezekiah stripped the doors of the Lord’s temple, and the posts which Hezekiah king of Judah had plated.”

verses.zh: 亚述王从拉吉差遣他珥探、拉伯撒利，和拉伯沙基率领大军往耶路撒冷，到希西家王那里去。他们上到耶路撒冷，就站在上池的水沟旁，在漂布地的大路上。
verses.en: The king of Assyria sent his commanding general, the chief eunuch, and the chief adviser[NOTE:1] from Lachish to King Hezekiah in Jerusalem,[NOTE:2] along with a large army. They went up and arrived at Jerusalem. They went[NOTE:3] and stood at the conduit of the upper pool which is located on the road to the field where they wash and dry cloth.[NOTE:4]
notes: For a discussion of these titles see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 229-30.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “and they went up and came.”
Heb “the field of the fuller.”

verses.zh: 他们呼叫王的时候，就有希勒家的儿子家宰以利亚敬，并书记舍伯那和亚萨的儿子史官约亚，出来见他们。
verses.en: They summoned the king, so Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace supervisor, accompanied by Shebna, the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph, the secretary, went out to meet them.

verses.zh: 拉伯沙基说：「你们去告诉希西家说，亚述大王如此说：『你所倚靠的有甚么可仗赖的呢？
verses.en: The chief adviser said to them, “Tell Hezekiah: ‘This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: “What is your source of confidence?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “What is this object of trust in which you are trusting?”

verses.zh: 你说有打仗的计谋和能力，我看不过是虚话。你到底倚靠谁才背叛我呢？
verses.en: Your claim to have a strategy and military strength is just empty talk.[NOTE:1] In whom are you trusting that you would dare to rebel against me?
notes: Heb “you say only a word of lips, counsel and might for battle.” Sennacherib’s message appears to be in broken Hebrew at this point. The phrase “word of lips” refers to mere or empty talk in Prov 14:23.

verses.zh: 看哪，你所倚靠的埃及是那压伤的苇杖；人若靠这杖，就必刺透他的手。埃及王法老向一切倚靠他的人也是这样。
verses.en: Now look, you must be trusting in Egypt, that splintered reed staff. If a man leans for support on it, it punctures his hand and wounds him. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt does to all who trust in him.

verses.zh: 你们若对我说：我们倚靠耶和华―我们的　神，希西家岂不是将　神的邱坛和祭坛废去，且对犹大和耶路撒冷的人说：你们当在耶路撒冷这坛前敬拜吗？
verses.en: Perhaps you will tell me, ‘We are trusting in the Lord our God.’ But Hezekiah is the one who eliminated his high places and altars and then told the people of Judah and Jerusalem, ‘You must worship at this altar in Jerusalem.’

verses.zh: 现在你把当头给我主亚述王，我给你二千匹马，看你这一面骑马的人够不够。
verses.en: Now make a deal[NOTE:1] with my master the king of Assyria, and I will give you 2,000 horses, provided you can find enough riders for them.
notes: Heb “exchange pledges.”

verses.zh: 若不然，怎能打败我主臣仆中最小的军长呢？你竟倚靠埃及的战车马兵吗？
verses.en: Certainly you will not refuse one of my master’s minor officials and trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “How can you turn back the face of an official [from among] the least of my master’s servants and trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?” In vv. 23-24 the chief adviser develops further the argument begun in v. 21. His reasoning seems to be as follows: “In your weakened condition you obviously need military strength. Agree to the king’s terms and I will personally give you more horses than you are capable of outfitting. If I, a mere minor official, am capable of giving you such military might, just think what power the king has. There is no way the Egyptians can match our strength. It makes much better sense to deal with us.”

verses.zh: 现在我上来攻击毁灭这地，岂没有耶和华的意思吗？耶和华吩咐我说：你上去攻击毁灭这地吧！』」
verses.en: Furthermore it was by the command of the Lord that I marched up against this place to destroy it. The Lord told me, ‘March up[NOTE:1] against this land and destroy it.’”’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Go up.”

In v. 25 the chief adviser develops further the argument begun in v. 22. He claims that Hezekiah has offended the Lord and that the Lord has commissioned Assyria as his instrument of discipline and judgment.

verses.zh: 希勒家的儿子以利亚敬和舍伯那，并约亚，对拉伯沙基说：「求你用亚兰言语和仆人说话，因为我们懂得；不要用犹大言语和我们说话，达到城上百姓的耳中。」
verses.en: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to the chief adviser, “Speak to your servants in Aramaic,[NOTE:1] for we understand it. Don’t speak with us in the Judahite dialect[NOTE:2] in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.”
notes: Aramaic was the diplomatic language of the empire.
Or “Hebrew.”

verses.zh: 拉伯沙基说：「我主差遣我来，岂是单对你和你的主说这些话吗？不也是对这些坐在城上、要与你们一同吃自己粪、喝自己尿的人说吗？」
verses.en: But the chief adviser said to them, “My master did not send me to speak these words only to your master and to you.[NOTE:1] His message is also for the men who sit on the wall, for they will eat their own excrement and drink their own urine along with you.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “To your master and to you did my master send me to speak these words?” The rhetorical question expects a negative answer.

Heb “[Is it] not [also] to the men…?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Yes, it is.”sn The chief adviser alludes to the horrible reality of siege warfare, when the starving people in the besieged city would resort to eating and drinking anything to stay alive.

verses.zh: 于是拉伯沙基站着，用犹大言语大声喊着说：「你们当听亚述大王的话！
verses.en: The chief adviser then stood there and called out loudly in the Judahite dialect,[NOTE:1] “Listen to the message of the great king, the king of Assyria.
notes: The Hebrew text also has, “and he spoke and said.”

verses.zh: 王如此说：『你们不要被希西家欺哄了；因他不能救你们脱离我的手。
verses.en: This is what the king says: ‘Don’t let Hezekiah mislead you, for he is not able to rescue you from my hand![NOTE:1]
notes: The MT has “his hand,” but this is due to graphic confusion of vav (ו) and yod (י). The translation reads “my hand,” along with many medieval Hebrew mss, the LXX, Syriac Peshitta, Targum, and Vulgate.

verses.zh: 也不要听希西家使你们倚靠耶和华，说耶和华必要拯救我们，这城必不交在亚述王的手中。』
verses.en: Don’t let Hezekiah talk you into trusting in the Lord when he says, “The Lord will certainly rescue us; this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.”

verses.zh: 不要听希西家的话！因亚述王如此说：『你们要与我和好，出来投降我，各人就可以吃自己葡萄树和无花果树的果子，喝自己井里的水。
verses.en: Don’t listen to Hezekiah!’ For this is what the king of Assyria says, ‘Send me a token of your submission and surrender to me.[NOTE:1] Then each of you may eat from his own vine and fig tree and drink water from his own cistern,
notes: Heb “make with me a blessing and come out to me.”

verses.zh: 等我来领你们到一个地方与你们本地一样，就是有五谷和新酒之地，有粮食和葡萄园之地，有橄榄树和蜂蜜之地，好使你们存活，不至于死。希西家劝导你们，说耶和华必拯救我们；你们不要听他的话。
verses.en: until I come and take you to a land just like your own—a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive oil and honey. Then you will live and not die. Don’t listen to Hezekiah, for he is misleading you when he says, “The Lord will rescue us.”

verses.zh: 列国的神有哪一个救他本国脱离亚述王的手呢？
verses.en: Have any of the gods of the nations actually rescued his land from the power of the king of Assyria?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Have the gods of the nations really rescued, each his land, from the hand of the king of Assyria?” The infinitive absolute lends emphasis to the main verb. The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course not!”

verses.zh: 哈马、亚珥拔的神在哪里呢？西法瓦音、希拿、以瓦的神在哪里呢？他们曾救撒马利亚脱离我的手吗？
verses.en: Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?[NOTE:1] Indeed, did any gods rescue Samaria[NOTE:2] from my power?[NOTE:3]
notes: The parallel passage in Isa 36:19 omits “Hena and Ivvah.” The rhetorical questions in v. 34a suggest the answer, “Nowhere, they seem to have disappeared in the face of Assyria’s might.”
For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

Heb “that they rescued Samaria from my hand?” But this gives the impression that the gods of Sepharvaim were responsible for protecting Samaria, which is obviously not the case. The implied subject of the plural verb “rescued” must be the generic “gods of the nations/lands” (vv. 33, 35).

verses.zh: 这些国的神有谁曾救自己的国脱离我的手呢？难道耶和华能救耶路撒冷脱离我的手吗？』」
verses.en: Who among all the gods of the lands has rescued their lands from my power? So how can the Lord rescue Jerusalem from my power?’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “that the Lord might rescue Jerusalem from my hand?” The logic runs as follows: Since no god has ever been able to withstand the Assyrian onslaught, how can the people of Jerusalem possibly think the Lord will rescue them?

verses.zh: 百姓静默不言，并不回答一句，因为王曾吩咐说：「不要回答他。」
verses.en: The people were silent and did not respond, for the king had ordered, “Don’t respond to him.”

verses.zh: 当下，希勒家的儿子家宰以利亚敬和书记舍伯那，并亚萨的儿子史官约亚，都撕裂衣服，来到希西家那里，将拉伯沙基的话告诉了他。
verses.en: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace supervisor, accompanied by Shebna the scribe and Joah son of Asaph, the secretary, went to Hezekiah with their clothes torn[NOTE:1] and reported to him what the chief adviser had said.
notes: As a sign of grief and mourning.
